take: Mogshade makes golf headcovers by hand in Portugal, and the name tells you everything about the sensibility: it comes from an old English dialect word for the play of light and shadow — sun filtering through leaves onto the course. The whole operation runs on what the brand calls ethical circularity. Everything is made to order (current lead time is about three weeks), which means no overproduction, and the fabrics are natural, recycled, upcycled, offcut, or deadstock — including rescued wool from the Serra da Estrela mountain factories that anchors the Re.Weave and Churra collections. Every piece is slightly different because the fabric was never mass-produced; what you get is what's left from the loom.
story_extra: Since we first covered them in June, the catalog has kept moving — small handmade batches sell out fast here, which is half the appeal. The Depeche Golf magazine collab dropped in August with a special-edition headcover. The wall art program is real now: hand-tufted wool posters of imagined holes and pin sheets that take eight weeks to make. There's an Ocean Bottle collab, sweats, and socks. And for American readers, the practical note: since June, US orders ship with import duties and customs fees already included.

The other thing that sets Mogshade apart is how much company it keeps. For a one-workshop operation, the collab sheet reads like a map of independent golf: an artist series with Fabricaal that turned headcovers into canvases, a capsule with IGG that sold through in weeks, Projeto Serra — a tribute to the brand's home mountains, down to the "Ovelha Preta" black-sheep cover — and an "On Set with Manors" edit curated with the London golfwear brand. Add the Depeche Golf magazine bundle, the Ocean Bottle, a Fiumani cap, and the early Parmore run that was capped at 50 pieces, and you get the picture: almost everything they touch disappears. There's also a custom-made program if you want a cover built to your spec from whatever's on the shelf that month.
Updated, August 2026 — we re-checked every piece below against the current catalog, pruned what's sold out, and added twelve new items from the workshop.
